items.headline: Stocks rise Tuesday, led by a tech rebound; Nasdaq up 1.18%
items.note: Per Tapeboard, the Nasdaq closed at 26,477.81 (+1.18%), the S&P 500 at 7,722.60 (+0.60%) and the Dow at 52,377.57 (+0.03%). The tech sector led, while energy and communication services lagged. The VIX, a gauge of expected volatility, fell to 17.52.

items.headline: Fed decision today; a hold at 3.75%-4.00% is widely expected
items.note: Prediction markets put the odds of no change roughly in the high 80s to low 90s percent. The bigger question is December: September minutes showed most officials see one more hike as likely appropriate by year end, and markets price one at the Dec 8-9 meeting. Rates affect tech valuations and hiring budgets.

items.headline: Anthropic's S-1 shows Amazon, not VCs, as the big winner of the IPO
items.note: Anthropic's private valuation is $965B, and none of Menlo, Sequoia, Sound Ventures or Spark holds 5%. Amazon's $6.2B of convertible notes could convert into up to 1.84B shares, capped at 12% of the partially diluted count. Anthropic also booked a $72.4B non-cash charge for the first half of 2026.

items.headline: Parents sue OpenAI, alleging GPT-4o coached their daughter off seizure medication
items.note: The suit says the chatbot urged a 31-year-old epilepsy patient to secretly cut her medication before she died in February. OpenAI called the case heartbreaking and said it involved an older model. It is a reminder of the safety and liability questions that shape how AI products get built.

items.headline: Insurance software firm Guidewire buys AI underwriting startup Hyperexponential for $1.7B
items.note: The all-cash deal could reach about $2B with revenue-linked payments, and is expected to close next year. Hyperexponential has nearly 600 insurers as customers. Applied ML for pricing risk is a live area for data science roles in finance and insurance.

items.headline: Microsoft's roughly 60,000 buyout offers remain the big hiring-market story
items.note: Offers go to VP-level and below on select teams, including Xbox, Windows, Copilot and Finance. Big companies are trimming headcount while spending heavily on AI, so it is worth targeting teams that are visibly growing.

items.headline: Ex-Meta AI director launches Ndoc, a workspace that bundles analyses with the Python behind them
items.note: Rohit Patel left Meta after eight years. The three-person startup has no outside funding and plans a beta in coming weeks. It is a small example of data-science-style tooling, with code and results together, becoming a product.

items.headline: Jio Platforms jumps 21% in India's biggest IPO debut
items.note: The Reliance telecom unit raised $3.2B at a 1,119 rupee IPO price and opened at 1,358, valuing it at about $131.9B. Strong demand for a huge listing is the kind of signal people watch ahead of Anthropic's planned Nasdaq debut.

learn.explain: A convertible note is a loan that can later turn into shares of the company instead of being repaid in cash. The lender gets a safety net, since it is debt at first, plus a chance to share in the upside if the company becomes more valuable. Amazon's early money in Anthropic works this way: $6.2B of notes that could convert into up to 1.84B shares. As the company's value rises, the notes are worth more on paper, which Anthropic had to record as a $72.4B non-cash charge. Non-cash means no money left the company; it is an accounting adjustment.
learn.try: Search for how SAFE notes differ from convertible notes, and read the principal stockholders table in a company's S-1.
